body.heading: Pick your exhibit
paragraphs: A kettle, a bicycle bell, a favourite mug, a door key. The more ordinary the object, the better the game, because the point is discovering how much story a plain thing can hold.
Begin with observation alone: weight, materials, marks of wear, sounds it makes, the small design decisions someone made about it long ago.

body.heading: Write its label
paragraphs: Museums explain objects with short labels. Write one for yours: what it is, roughly when and where it was made, what it is for, and one interesting thing most people would miss.

Then add the personal gallery: where this object has been, what it has witnessed, why this one matters to you. You have just practised history, science and storytelling on a mug, which is a fine afternoon's work.

takeaway: Give one ordinary object the museum treatment and read the story it was hiding.
